title: unified-observability-data-safeguard-orchestrator-trace-metric-log-flow
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Overview: Build a unified data-governance orchestrator that centralizes PII redaction, tenant-aware retention, and RBAC/access-logging for traces, metrics, and log pipelines. This ticket implements the core runtime hooks, pipeline adapters, and dashboard surface so platform and tenant owners can configure safeguards without touching individual agents.

Motivation: Current scrubbing is fragmented across collectors and ingestion adapters which causes inconsistent masking, compliance gaps, and operational overhead for audits. High-level goals are: 1) consistent field-level redaction/pseudonymization across traces/logs/metrics, 2) tenant-scoped retention tiers with just-in-time reveal audit trail, 3) immutable access logs for observability data queries and dashboard views, and 4) minimal latency regression for live tracing and dashboards.

Scope: 1) tracing hooks in the agent SDKs to emit sanitized span payloads and access annotations, 2) an orchestrator service (stateless) that applies policy-driven scrubbing and routing decisions for metrics and logs, 3) a retention coordinator that enforces TTLs per-tenant and per-data-class, 4) RBAC layer integration with identity service for query-level logging, and 5) dashboard instrumentation that surfaces redaction/retention status and latency/error breakdowns.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered: 
- Centralized scrub orchestrator vs per-collector scrubber: we chose a hybrid pattern. Lightweight agent-level scrubs (remove raw PII patterns) minimize egress of clearly sensitive tokens; complex, policy-driven transforms live in the orchestrator to enable rapid policy changes without agent upgrades.
- Field-level pseudonymization: reversible tokenization with tenant-scoped keys for just-in-time reveal on investigatory workflows. Reversible approach chosen over irreversible hashing to support debugging and incident replay under strict audit controls. This increases attack surface, so KMS/HSM integration and key-rotation policies are mandatory.
- Performance: Scrubbing must not add >5ms median per-trace hop in p95 workloads. We'll prefer streaming transforms using compiled regex and heuristic classifiers; fall back to async enrichment where strict TTL/retention enforcement is required.
- Retention tiers: hot (30 days), warm (90 days), cold (365 days) by default with tenant overrides. Tier transitions will be background jobs to keep ingest path fast.

Acceptance criteria: 
- All new traces emitted by instrumented services include redaction metadata and pass a scrubbed canonicalizer in CI tests.
- Orchestrator applies tenant policies and logs each transformation to an immutable access audit with actor, policy-id, pre/post-digest, and timestamp.
- RBAC-enforced query paths write query-level access log entries to the audit stream. Query logs are retained 365 days and accessible to security during investigations.
- Dashboard surfaces per-tenant PII-scrub coverage, retention tier, and related latency/error deltas in the last 24h and 7d.
- End-to-end canary against 10% of traffic for two weeks with no regression in SLOs (99th percentile tail latency for traces and dashboard load).

Implementation plan: 
1) Agents: add tracing hooks and opt-in lightweight scrubbing (Anika). Producer PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/agents/pull/1286.
2) Orchestrator service: proto for policy engine, transform registry, and scrub pipeline; deploy to staging cluster behind feature flag. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Observability+Data+Safeguard+Orchestrator.
3) Retention coordinator: background batch jobs to move data to cold tier and enforce TTL deletions; use tenancy metadata in object store.
4) RBAC integration: connect orchestrator to IdP and token introspection endpoint; add query-level audit hooks in the query gateway.
5) Dashboards: add a new observability governance panel to Console; dashboard spec: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs-governance/pii-coverage.
6) Canary & rollout: enable feature flag per-tenant, monitor SLOs, iterate.

Migration/backfill: We will run a policy-based pass over 60 days of hot data to apply canonical redaction and populate transformation ledger. Backfill will run in low-load windows and append audit entries. A data-forensics snapshot process will be available for security-led reveals (requires approval workflow).

Security/compliance controls:
- Keys stored in KMS with HSM-backed rotation.
- Immutable access ledger backed by append-only storage with signed digests.
- SOC2/GDPR mapping for each policy (Confluence mapping linked).

Metrics & observability for this work: 
- Instrument orchestration latency histogram, transform-failure rate, per-tenant scrub-coverage, RTT impact to span enrichment.
- Add dashboard panels for latency/error deltas and a runbook link to incident playbook.

Rollout risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Unintended data loss if policies misconfigured. Mitigation: dry-run mode with no-op transforms and delta reporting for 2 weeks before enforcement.
- Risk: Latency regressions. Mitigation: circuit-breaker to bypass orchestrator for slow tenants and fallback to best-effort scrubbing.
- Risk: Key compromise. Mitigation: key-rotation, split knowledge for reveal flow, and mandatory security review.

Delivery milestones: 
- 2026-02-28: agent PR opened and initial unit tests (done).
- 2026-03-10: orchestrator prototype deployed to staging (this ticket milestone).
- 2026-03-18: retention coordinator PoC and dashboard panels in staging.
- 2026-03-31: canary rollout to 10% tenants and security sign-off.

Out-of-scope: log ingestion format changes for third-party customers, deep-packet inspection, and application-level consent management (handled by product).
acceptance_criteria: Instrumented traces include redaction metadata and pass CI scrub canonicalizer
Orchestrator logs every transformation to immutable audit with actor and policy-id
RBAC query paths produce immutable access logs retained 365 days
Console dashboard shows per-tenant PII-scrub coverage and latency/error deltas
Canary 10% traffic for 2 weeks with no SLO regressions
